topic: Luke Aikins no-parachute skydive net engineering
title: He Jumped From 25,000 Feet With No Parachute — And Lived
description: AI-narrated commentary on the 2016 stunt where Luke Aikins skydived from 25,000 feet with no parachute and landed safely in a net. This is original commentary on the engineering behind it, not the source footage. #shorts #skydiving #engineering

beats.text: In 2016 a man jumped from four miles up with zero parachute — and lived.
Luke Aikins fell for two minutes at over 120 miles an hour. No gear. No backup chute.
beats.broll_query: skydiver falling fast motion blur sky

beats.text: His plan wasn't luck. It was a 100-foot net, engineered and tested for years before he stepped on the plane.
The net absorbed the impact by spreading force across thousands of fibers, turning a lethal stop into a controlled slowdown.
beats.broll_query: fabric fiber weave closeup slow motion

beats.text: Every earlier jump was a crash-test dummy, then stunt doubles, then finally him.
The real danger wasn't the fall. It was missing the net's center by even a few feet.
He landed dead center, stood up, and walked away.
beats.broll_query: person standing up walking away triumphant

beats.text: Would you trust years of testing over a parachute, or does that still sound like a coin flip? Let me know.
